title: Polygon layer

configuration.note: Ring closure, winding and CRS84 bounds are checked when the file is read. What is NOT checkable here is whether the lines are where the author meant them to be: a traced territory is a reading of a printed wash, and experiment 145 records that as not established. The acquisition parameters are stated and never inferred: a kind is chosen from a closed list, the vertex threshold defaults to nothing, and the margin defaults to zero. An acquired layer carries `dataRef`, so its features are held once on the device rather than in the workflow.

ports.note: One OPTIONAL input, `area`, which scopes acquisition rather than enabling the widget: connected, it supplies the bounding box and the country a published OpenStreetMap extract is read for, which is what `network_input` already does with the same port. Absent, the widget still reads a GeoJSON file as published, so `required` stays empty and this remains an input-stage widget -- `INPUT_STAGE` is derived from `required`, not from `optional`, so the palette's blank-canvas behaviour is unchanged. At run time the port is checked for one thing: a layer whose retrieval box no longer covers the connected area is REFUSED, because acquisition happens at import and a study area nudged afterwards leaves a layer that provably holds no features for part of it. Emits the existing `polygons` port type, as before.

ontology.note: No mapping to an external vocabulary yet. The receipt states the file, its digest, the feature count, the property each feature was named by, and that nothing was clipped, simplified or reprojected. An acquired layer adds no terms of its own: its licence and retrieval are recorded through `input-provenance.ts`, whose `fw:licence`, `fw:retrievedFrom` and `fw:retrievedAt` are already declared and whose KNOWN_OBLIGATIONS already carries `ODbL-1.0` with its attribution and share-alike obligation. Asserting a parallel vocabulary here would have earned a receipt nothing else reads.

changes: Choose features: a modal viewer listing every feature the read returned beside a map of them. Select a row and its polygon is marked; clear its box and it leaves the layer. The practitioner, 2026-10-29, after a read of Greater London's water areas returned 606 features where two were wanted: "Perhaps the polygon input can have a polygon viewer that has polygons in view and the rows associated with them. If I click on the row the polygon is highlighted. And then I can hide it."

It replaced a design that filtered at read time by a named property and a list of values. You cannot name values you have not seen, and a read of OpenStreetMap water areas returns ponds, basins and a boating lake whose names nobody knows in advance.

Hidden rather than deleted, by id. The read is unchanged and repeatable, the layer carries what survives, and fw:featuresRead and fw:featuresSetAside record the choice in the receipt -- a layer of two drawn from a read of 606 is a decision a reader of the evidence has to be able to see.
Setting every feature aside is refused: a layer that holds nothing is not a layer.

The feature cap is gone. MAX_LAYER_FEATURES refused a layer by how many features it held, on the grounds that past it "a layer is a basemap rather than a study's own geometry" -- a definition asserted rather than a constraint measured -- and on a vertex budget that is checked separately, on its real total. It refused 606 water features from an extract already on the practitioner's own disk. What remains refuses on vertices, which is the thing that costs.
A layer is named after its node where it has no name of its own, so a collected layer no longer reaches stack_polygons anonymous.

evidence.note: Unit tested against the three MultiPolygon territories the South London repository ships, which is the layer the widget was built for: 153, 128 and 107 vertices across six rings, every vertex preserved, the attributes carried as published, and the three supply categories read from the property the practitioner named. The HOLES are asserted explicitly, because they are what makes reading as published worth enforcing: Lambeth's territory is one part of three rings -- an outer boundary of 107 positions and two interior rings of 9 and 12 -- so there are enclaves inside the Lambeth zone that Lambeth did not supply, which no count of features reveals and which a simplifier would take first. Refusals covered: coordinates outside CRS84 bounds (easting and northing in metres, which is what an export from a projected CRS gives), a geometry that is not a polygon, an unclosed ring, a named property no feature carries, a file that is not a FeatureCollection, an empty one, and one larger than a study's own geometry. What this does not establish is whether the traced lines are where Snow's printed wash actually was: the geometry is a reading of a colour boundary on a scanned plate, and experiment 145 records it as a reading rather than a measurement. The acquisition half is tested against a .osm.pbf the test writes itself, there being no fixture in this repository and no decode test for the street engine either: eight cases over tag matching, multipolygon assembly from reversed fragments, the box, the vertex threshold, the measured refusal and the granularity assumption. Three further cases cover the port -- that a layer read for the study area runs and states its obligation, that one read for a different area is refused by name, and that a plain read file is unaffected. Verified end to end against the real extract: all six water relations the hand-built South London partition used are present and the one outside the box is excluded.
